releases.body:
### Picker policy: Perun's own agents stay in their lane

* New `perun/agent_policy.py`, consumed by `/api/agents?surface=` with
  **default-deny**: a request without a surface gets the project rules, so a
  picker that forgets to name its surface fails closed.
  * project (default) - built-ins + agents assigned globally or to that project
  * control - `perun-orchestrator` + built-ins
  * perunchat - the room persona only
  * docs - `perun-docs` only
  * all - unfiltered, explicit
* The dashboard passes its surface explicitly: the orchestrator panel and the
  Settings orchestrator field use `control`, the PerunChat chat persona uses
  `perunchat`. Run, the wizard, coroutines and project surfaces now never offer
  `perun-*`.
* Assignment decisions come from the manifest (`assignments_map()`), so a project
  copy outside the global dirs still counts as assigned.
* Unassigning an agent's **last** placement no longer deletes it: it moves back to
  the library, unassigned, exactly like a fresh install. Only **Remove** deletes.
* Project panel readability: the agent list uses the dark palette (it was black
  text on a dark background), and when every installed agent is global the panel
  says so instead of showing a fully locked list - that is the state where
  nothing is tickable, because the project already inherits everything.

### Installs are unassigned until you place them

* The dashboard's **Install selected** now writes to Perun's **library**
  (`PERUN_HOME/agents/library/`), which OpenCode never reads. A new agent appears
  in no TUI until you assign it - the opt-in model, finally end to end.
  Programmatic `install()` keeps its global default, so nothing else changes.
* Settings -> Installed shows **"N unassigned"** with **Assign all globally**, and
  each row now reads `global`, `project only` or `unassigned`.
* `assign` sources from the library copy, so a library agent can be placed in a
  project or globally; the library file stays as the master and is not counted
  against the registration ceiling (OpenCode never loads it).
* `installed()` returns the `unassigned` list, and `available()` counts a library
  agent as installed.
* Library files are discovered like any other copy (`assignment: "library"`), so
  promote, remove and the assignment fan-out work on them unchanged.

### Assignment refuses Perun's own agents

* `assign` now checks the target through the same protection as every other
  mutation: assigning `perun-orchestrator`, `perun-docs`, `perunchat` or any
  other agent Perun owns is refused with *"a Perun agent; the roster never
  touches it"* instead of reporting a successful assignment.
* Found by the release verification, not by a test: the guard existed for
  remove/promote but not for placement.

### Assign roster agents to projects

* Placement is now explicit. A new `perun/agent_assignments.py` owns it: a copy
  in the global agents directory is a **global** assignment, a copy under
  `<project>/.opencode/agents/` is a **project** assignment, and both are derived
  from where the file lives (the only truth OpenCode reads).
* Settings -> Agent roster -> Installed shows each agent's assignment and a
  **Global** toggle; **Remove** now removes the agent everywhere it is assigned.
* Project config -> **Agents in this project**: tick the agents that project's TUI
  should offer. Globally assigned agents are inherited and shown locked.
* Project copies are **local-only**: the agents directory gets a `.gitignore`
  containing `*`, so `git status` stays clean. Every removal keeps a backup.
* Assigning an agent that is already global to a project is a no-op; unassign and
  remove refuse a copy edited since install.
* `promote` fans the new `mode:` out to every copy.
* API: `POST /api/agent-catalog/{assign,unassign}`, `remove {slug}`. CLI:
  `perun agent-catalog assign|unassign <slug...> --to global|project:<slug>`.
* Install still writes globally in this release; the library/unassigned default
  ships next, with the post-install assign prompt.

### Roster edge cases from the audit

* `promote` / `accept` map an unreadable agent file to a 400 (`could not read …`)
  instead of letting an `OSError` escape as a 500 traceback.
* `_agent_mode` scans 80 frontmatter lines (matching the discovery parser), so a
  long frontmatter still reports its mode and the toggle/badge stay honest.
* Two unit cases pin the edges: an unknown slug is rejected, and an agent with no
  `mode:` reports an empty mode.

### Promote a roster agent from the dashboard

* Settings → Agent roster → **Installed** gains a per-agent **Make primary ⇄
  Primary** toggle. It sets `mode: all`: the agent becomes selectable in Run, the
  Agent Console and the project/coroutine pickers, and stays delegable. One click
  puts it back to `subagent`.
* `promote` now **refuses a file edited since it was installed** instead of
  silently re-baselining the edits. An **Accept** action on the row re-baselines a
  deliberate edit, which is what unblocks promoting or removing it.
* `installed()` reports each agent's current `mode`, read from the file (cached by
  mtime/size and invalidated on every write) rather than from the manifest.
* A `primary` badge and a **Primary only** filter, and the footer now says
  OpenCode picks up promotions as well as installs and removals.
* The toggle rests on a measurement, not an assumption: `perun-orchestrator` is a
  file-based agent with `mode: primary` and its recorded runs complete, so
  `--agent` accepts a file-based non-subagent agent.
* New `_target_for()` resolves an agent by path or slug; it is the single place
  the assignment work will redirect to the library copy.

### The ceiling is measured again, and MCP startup no longer blocks

* The agent ceiling was **stale**. Upstream's "~119" comes from an old report;
  measured on OpenCode v2.2.5 with `opencode debug agents --standalone`, **307**
  agents registered from 300 files with nothing dropped, tracking 1:1 from 110 to
  300. The default is now **300**, the refusal names the fix
  (`perun agent-catalog limit <n>`), and the Settings card keeps the message on
  screen instead of letting a toast disappear.
* `mcp/perun_mcp.py` no longer does slow work before answering the stdio
  handshake. Control-project registration and handbook indexing (which embeds
  with a 180 s request timeout) moved to a daemon thread; `init_db()` stays
  synchronous because every tool needs it and it is cheap DDL. This is the
  `mcp connect failed: Request timed out` seen in OpenCode's log after ~184 s —
  the handshake was waiting on an embedding call.

### Faster listing, and a safer bulk uninstall

* File hashes are cached by `(mtime_ns, size)`, so the Settings card no longer
  re-reads every agent file on each render; any writer invalidates the entry it
  touches. A same-size, same-timestamp rewrite is the only case it could miss.
* `remove_many` runs in **one** manifest transaction: removing a 66-agent
  division is one write instead of 66, and a failure midway keeps every earlier
  removal.
* `remove --division` supports `--dry-run` (list, change nothing) and needs
  `--yes` to actually delete; the API takes `dry_run` too.
* The Installed list gains a division filter, and an `unlisted` agent (adopted,
  hash still matching) now offers **Remove** instead of only **Forget**.

### Uninstall stays inside the scope you named

* `remove --division <name> --project <slug>` (and the equivalent API call) now
  removes only that project's copies. It previously matched every agent of the
  division, including the machine-wide ones, because the scope was not part of
  the filter.
* `POST /api/agent-catalog/remove` with an empty `paths` list is a clear 400
  (*"choose agents (paths) or a division"*) instead of falling through to a
  single-file removal of the empty path.

### Uninstall from the dashboard, and Perun's own agents are untouchable

* Settings → **Agent roster** → **Installed** lists every installed agent with a
  **Remove** button, a per-division removal chip (*Remove engineering (66)*), and
  **Forget** for an edited one — an edited file is never deleted. Removal keeps a
  backup, and OpenCode picks up installs and removals on its next start.
* `GET /api/agent-catalog/installed` returns compact rows (no descriptions) and
  `POST /api/agent-catalog/remove` accepts `path`, `paths` or `division`. CLI:
  `perun agent-catalog installed`, `perun agent-catalog remove --division <name>`.
* **Perun's own agents are explicitly protected.** `perun-*` templates and the
  chat persona can no longer be adopted, installed over, promoted or deleted by
  the catalogue, and are never listed. Before, that held only because they are
  not in the roster index — an accident, not a rule.
* The roster stays opt-in: nothing is installed by default, and every install is
  removable from the same card.
* The runtime baseline is only applied when the runtime reports at least one of
  Perun's roster files; if it is looking at another directory the two counts
  describe different machines, and the guard falls back to counting files
  (`slots.baseline_source` says which).
